release_review_billing:
VERDICT: Genuine improvement

WHAT THE OFFICIAL METRIC SAYS: billing containment rose from 71.6% to 80.7% post-v2 (+9.0pp, z=7.83, p<0.001) -- a large, highly significant jump in the agent's self-reported resolution rate.

WHAT THE TRUE METRIC SAYS: reopen-adjusted true containment also rose significantly, 68.1% to 75.9% (+7.8pp, z=6.42, p<0.001) -- almost the same magnitude as the official lift, with reopen rate essentially flat (4.95% to 5.92%). The official number is not being inflated by a reopen problem here; it reflects a real improvement in outcomes.

COST IMPACT: average cost per billing ticket actually FELL, $2.50 to $1.93, driven by fewer costly human escalations -- a genuine win on both quality and cost.

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Ship as a confirmed win. No further investigation needed; consider this category a template for what a well-targeted containment improvement looks like when validating other categories' releases.
release_review_technical:
VERDICT: Genuine improvement

WHAT THE OFFICIAL METRIC SAYS: technical containment rose from 60.2% to 67.0% post-v2 (+6.75pp, z=4.99, p<0.001).

WHAT THE TRUE METRIC SAYS: true containment rose by a very similar amount, 55.1% to 62.7% (+7.54pp, z=5.45, p<0.001), and reopen rate actually improved slightly (8.44% to 6.40%) rather than worsening -- so this category's official improvement is fully corroborated by the true outcome metric, not inflated by it.

COST IMPACT: average cost per technical ticket fell from $3.51 to $2.92, consistent with fewer human escalations and no meaningful increase in reopen-driven rework cost.

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Ship as a confirmed win, same as billing. Worth understanding what specifically changed in the v2 technical-support flow, since it appears to be a genuinely more capable resolution path rather than a policy change that merely defers cost or risk.
release_review_shipping:
VERDICT: No significant change

WHAT THE OFFICIAL METRIC SAYS: shipping's official containment moved from 69.1% to 67.8% post-v2, a small decline that is NOT statistically significant (z=-0.84, p=0.40).

WHAT THE TRUE METRIC SAYS: true containment also shows no significant change (65.0% to 63.5%, z=-0.91, p=0.36), and reopen rate is essentially flat (6.0% to 6.3%).

COST IMPACT: average cost per shipping ticket is flat ($2.75 to $2.74), consistent with no real change in resolution behavior for this category.

RECOMMENDED ACTION: No action needed. Shipping is behaving as a reasonable control group for this release -- the v2 changes that helped billing and technical don't appear to have touched shipping's resolution logic at all, which is useful context for interpreting the other three categories' results as real, isolated effects rather than a broad seasonal shift.
release_review_account_recovery:
VERDICT: False improvement -- metric-gaming risk, not a real win

WHAT THE OFFICIAL METRIC SAYS: account_recovery's official containment jumped from 55.7% to 76.0% post-v2 (+20.2pp, z=12.8, p<0.001) -- by far the largest official lift of any category, and the kind of number that would normally be reported as this release's headline success story.

WHAT THE TRUE METRIC SAYS: true (reopen-adjusted) containment is completely flat: 50.2% before, 50.2% after (-0.04pp, z=-0.02, p=0.98, not remotely significant). The entire apparent 20pp official gain is explained by the reopen rate exploding from 9.8% to 33.9% -- the v2 policy is letting the agent autonomously take account-recovery actions (password resets, security overrides) that often don't actually fix the customer's problem, so the ticket gets marked 'resolved' and then reopens. The official metric is being gamed by the policy change, not improved by it.

COST IMPACT: average cost per account_recovery ticket is roughly flat ($3.89 to $3.65) -- so this is not even delivering a cost benefit to offset the customer-experience cost of a 3.4x higher reopen rate. By both the true-outcome lens and the cost lens, this policy change has delivered nothing, despite what its own top-line metric claims.

RECOMMENDED ACTION: Do NOT report this as a containment win. Escalate to the team that shipped the autonomous account-action policy: either tighten the conditions under which the agent takes an autonomous action versus escalating, or add a post-action verification step before marking these tickets resolved. Until fixed, exclude account_recovery's official containment number from any external or leadership-facing 'agent performance improved' reporting -- it is actively misleading.
